eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models for August 22, 2026, in Kuala Lumpur indicate a peak temperature most likely in the 33–35°C range, aligning closely with the market's heavy weighting toward 34°C (61%) and 35°C (27%).** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug, WindBorne, the UK Met Office, and Yr.no, project daytime highs near 33°C (roughly 92°F) under partly cloudy to mostly sunny conditions, with afternoon dew points supporting heat indices above 37°C.

Kuala Lumpur’s equatorial location and ongoing southwest monsoon regime typically produce high humidity and scattered convection that caps daytime maxima, yet reduced cloud cover and light southeasterly winds on the 22nd favor greater solar heating. Earlier August observations already show a +1.8°C departure from the long-term monthly normal, with several days exceeding 35°C, providing context for traders pricing modest upside risk.

Official guidance from regional meteorological agencies emphasizes low precipitation probability (20–40%) during peak heating hours, limiting evaporative cooling and supporting the 34°C outcome as the mode. Upcoming afternoon model updates and any revisions to boundary-layer moisture could still shift the distribution, but current consensus keeps extremes below 36°C or above 33°C at low implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model guidance position 92–95°F as the most probable range for Denver’s August 22 high, reflecting above-normal late-summer warmth driven by a strong ridge of high pressure and downslope westerly flow. Recent observations show Denver exceeding seasonal normals (87°F average high) amid scattered thunderstorms that have failed to produce significant cooling, consistent with the 35.5% market-implied probability for 92–93°F and combined 43% for the adjacent bins. Traders weigh the risk of convective cooling or a modest trough passage that could cap temperatures near 90°F against the potential for clearer skies and stronger heating that pushes readings into the mid-90s. Updated model runs and NWS briefings expected within the next 12–24 hours will likely refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.

Recent activity from a low-pressure area that crossed Hainan and lingering systems near Taiwan has maintained this unsettled pattern through the weekend, preventing clearer skies that would otherwise push readings toward the upper end of the distribution. Model consensus and climatological context (August average high near 31 °C) therefore support the even probabilities across 28–32 °C, while the low odds for 33 °C or above reflect the cooling effect of widespread cloud and rain.  

Traders are effectively pricing the narrow window between thunderstorm timing and any brief afternoon clearing that could add or subtract a degree or two from the daily peak.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent tropical moisture influx and the remnants of weakened systems like Neneng, combined with potential steering influences from developing disturbances, are elevating cloud cover and precipitation chances over Manila for August 23. Official PAGASA monitoring and ensemble forecasts indicate scattered thunderstorms with 50-80% rain probabilities, which typically cap daytime maxima near 29-31°C (84-88°F) through evaporative cooling and reduced insolation. This aligns with climatological August norms but introduces downward pressure on peak readings relative to clearer periods earlier in the month. Traders are weighting the timing of any convective bursts, as delayed or lighter rainfall could allow brief warmer spikes toward 32°C before resolution criteria are met. Updated model runs from global agencies will refine these variables ahead of the 24-hour observation window.
